ref: DAR — Revelation ch. 17: Babylon, the Mother
title: Babylon, the Mother
voicePrompt: In your own words, explain how this chapter distinguishes the woman from the beast, why Rome is called the mother of harlots rather than the only Babylon, and how the seven heads and ten horns trace Rome's history toward its final judgment.

questions.stem: According to the chapter, what do the woman and the scarlet-colored beast on which she sits respectively symbolize?
options: The woman is the civil power and the beast is the church
The woman is the church (Roman Catholic) and the beast is the civil power that upholds her
Both the woman and the beast symbolize pagan Rome
The woman is true Israel and the beast is the Roman senate
questions.explanation: The text says the prophecy distinguishes between church and state: "the woman, the church, seated upon a scarlet-colored beast, the civil power, by which she is upheld, and which she controls and guides to her own ends, as a rider controls the animal upon which he is seated." The apostate woman is identified as a symbol of the Roman Catholic Church.

questions.stem: Why does the chapter argue that Rome is NOT Babylon to the exclusion of all other religious bodies?
options: Because Babylon is only a literal city, not a church
Because she is called the mother of harlots, which shows there are other apostate daughter organizations in the same family
Because the prophecy applies only to pagan Rome, not the church
Because the woman represents all of Protestantism, not Rome
questions.explanation: The text answers its own question "Is Rome, then, Babylon, to the exclusion of all other religious bodies?" with "No, from the fact that she is called the mother of harlots... which shows that there are other independent religious organizations that constitute the apostate daughters, and belong to the same great family."

questions.stem: According to the chapter, why did John "wonder with great admiration" when he saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints?
options: Because he had never seen persecution before in his life
Because he was surprised that a church professedly Christian was persecuting the followers of the Lamb, whereas all persecution he had witnessed had come from pagan Rome
Because he doubted the woman could ever be defeated
Because he could not identify which kings supported her
questions.explanation: The text explains the secret of his wonder: all the persecution he had witnessed had been from pagan Rome, the open enemy of Christ; "but when he looked forward, and saw a church professedly Christian persecuting the followers of the Lamb, and drunken with their blood, he could but wonder with great amazement."

questions.stem: The chapter describes the beast as one that "was, and is not, and yet is." What three phases of Rome does this represent?
options: Babylon, Medo-Persia, and Greece
Pagan Rome (was), the transition while nominally converted to Christianity (is not), and Rome degenerated into popery (yet is)
Republican Rome, imperial Rome, and Byzantine Rome
The kingly, consular, and dictatorial governments
questions.explanation: The text describes Rome in three phases: pagan Rome was a persecuting power ("the beast that was"); during the transition while the empire was nominally converted to Christianity it lost its persecuting character ("the beast that it was not"); then it degenerated into popery and again became bloodthirsty ("the beast that yet is").

questions.stem: The chapter explains the seven heads as seven kings or forms of government. Which form does it identify as the eighth head, and what intervened between the imperial and papal heads?
options: The consular head is the eighth; the dictatorship intervened
The papal head is the eighth; the Exarch of Ravenna, a short-lived head, intervened between the imperial and papal
The imperial head is the eighth; the triumvirate intervened
The decemvirate is the eighth; the kingly form intervened
questions.explanation: The text concludes "the papal head is the eighth, and that a head of short continuance intervened between the imperial and papal," identifying that head as the ruler who "for about the space of sixty years governed Rome under the title of the 'Exarch of Ravenna.'"

questions.stem: According to the chapter, what do the ten horns of the beast represent, and what is their final relationship to the harlot?
options: Ten Roman emperors who all support her forever
The ten kingdoms that arose out of the Roman empire, who once upheld the papacy but will finally hate the harlot, make her desolate, and burn her with fire
Ten apostles who remain faithful to the woman
Ten provinces that the woman herself governs without conflict
questions.explanation: The text says the ten horns "represent the ten kingdoms that arose out of the Roman empire," who at first were "unanimous in giving their support to the papacy," but per verse 16 they "shall hate the harlot, make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her with fire."

questions.stem: How does the chapter interpret the "waters" where the whore sits (verse 15)?
options: Literal seas and rivers of the Roman empire
Peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues
The false doctrines of the church
The blood of the martyrs
questions.explanation: The text points to verse 15 as "a plain definition of the Scripture symbol of waters; they denote peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues."

questions.stem: How does the chapter relate this chapter (Revelation 17) to the chapter that follows it?
options: Revelation 17 deals with the harlot daughters and the next chapter with the mother
This chapter has more especial reference to the old mother (Catholic Babylon), while the next deals with another great branch of Babylon, the harlot daughters
Both chapters describe only pagan Rome
The next chapter abandons the Babylon symbol entirely
questions.explanation: The closing paragraph states this chapter "has, naturally, more especial reference to the old mother, or Catholic Babylon. The next chapter... deals with the character and destiny of another great branch of Babylon, the harlot daughters."
